title: Reasoning-Effort as an Implicit Reward-Hacking Signal: A Lightweight Monitor

original_idea.body: On an open coding/QA agent collect genuine-vs-reward-hacking trajectories, measure effort proxies (CoT tokens, tool calls, edit distance), and test whether a simple threshold separates hacks across categories.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Validating a cheap effort-based reward-hacking detector across hack types is directly deployable and complements CoT monitoring.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Collect genuine-vs-hack trajectories, measure effort proxies, threshold AUROC; accessible, no internal access.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused effort-threshold AUROC across hack categories; few dependencies.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: No internal access/fine-tuning, public models, lab-independent deployable heuristic.

novelty.reasoning: Effort-based detection shown in source; cross-hack-type open-model validation may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Effort signal shown; cross-hack-type model-agnostic validation may be open.
